name: Soft Mashed Rice with Expressed Breast Milk
sinhala_name: මව්කිරෙන් පොඟවා පොඩි කළ බත්
household_portion: 2 to 3 teaspoons (can give more if the baby eats)
energy_enrichment: Moistened and enriched with expressed breast milk
preparation_steps: Wash raw white rice and cook until very soft and tender.
Mash thoroughly with a clean spoon to a smooth, lump-free semi-solid puree.
Express a small amount of breast milk using clean hands into a sterilized cup.
Add expressed breast milk to the warm mashed rice to adjust consistency and provide a familiar taste.
Feed patiently when the infant is alert, calm, and slightly hungry.
safety_precautions: Do not add any salt or sugar.
Feed with a clean small spoon in a quiet place without screen distractions.
Do not force-feed if the baby turns their head or shows signs of fullness.
developmental_rationale: Breast milk gives a familiar flavor to ease the baby's transition from liquid milk to the first taste of solid food.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Soft mashed rice mixed with expressed breast milk is the explicit FHB inception food on Day 1 (2–3 teaspoons, once a day).

name: Soft Mashed Rice (Early Progression)
sinhala_name: පොඩි කළ බත් (දින 2–3)
household_portion: Gradually increase the amount at each meal from 2–3 tsp baseline
preparation_steps: Cook white or red rice soft until grains burst easily.
Mash thoroughly with a clean spoon.
Moisten slightly with expressed breast milk or warm boiled water to create a soft semi-solid mash.
Offer 1 to 2 times a day after or between daytime breastfeeds.
safety_precautions: Ensure food is at body temperature before offering.
developmental_rationale: Helps the baby practice swallowing thicker textures while building feeding routines.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 2 to 3 of complementary feeding: soft mashed rice, 1 to 2 meals a day, gradually increasing amount.

name: Mashed Rice with Dhal Puree & Mashed Fruit
sinhala_name: පරිප්පු සමඟ පොඩි කළ බත්
household_portion: 3 to 4 teaspoons or more at a time + 1 teaspoon or more fruit
preparation_steps: Wash red lentils (dhal) thoroughly and boil until creamy and tender.
Mash dhal into a smooth puree.
Boil white or red rice until soft and mash with spoon.
Combine 3–4 tsp of soft rice and dhal puree.
Peel a ripe banana or papaya and mash 1 tsp smoothly to offer immediately after the rice meal.
safety_precautions: Strict single-food trial rule: Introduce one new food at a time for 2–3 continuous days.
developmental_rationale: Dhal introduces plant protein and iron, while fresh fruit introduces vitamin C which enhances iron absorption.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 4 to 6: mashed rice with dhal puree (3–4 tsp or more, twice a day) + 1 tsp mashed fruit.

name: Mashed Rice with Dhal & Whole Sprat Powder
sinhala_name: හාල්මැස්සන් කුඩු සමඟ පරිප්පු බත්
household_portion: Introductory portion building from 3–4 tsp towards 5–6 tsp + ~1 tsp sprat powder
preparation_steps: Prepare sprat powder according to FHB protocol: Wash dried sprats thoroughly without removing the head. Roast in a pan or dry. Grind whole into fine powder and store in clean dry bottle.
Cook rice and dhal together with thick coconut milk until soft.
Add about 1 teaspoon of sprat powder while cooking.
Mash together smoothly to a semi-solid paste, gradually increasing particle size day by day.
safety_precautions: Ensure sprats are ground finely without sharp bone fragments.
developmental_rationale: Animal-origin foods like sprats supply rich bioavailable iron and calcium needed for rapid brain growth in the first 2 years.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: FHB Sprat Preparation Protocol on booklet page 6 introduces whole sprat powder on days 7 to 9.

name: Mashed Rice with Steamed Sea Fish & Thick Coconut Milk
sinhala_name: මාළු සහ මිටිකිරි සමඟ පොඩි කළ බත්
household_portion: Building from 3–4 tsp towards 5–6 tsp twice daily + fruit
preparation_steps: Steam or boil fresh sea fish thoroughly.
Flake and inspect flesh with clean fingers to remove every single bone.
Cook soft rice and dhal with thick coconut milk.
Combine deboned fish flake with warm rice and dhal; mash into a soft semi-solid paste.
safety_precautions: Inspect fish with extreme vigilance to eliminate all bones.
developmental_rationale: Sea fish provides high-quality protein and essential fatty acids for neuromuscular and cognitive development.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Sea fish introduced on days 7 to 9 cooked with thick coconut milk.

name: Mashed Rice with Tender Chicken & Vegetable Oil
sinhala_name: කුකුල් මස් සමඟ පොඩි කළ බත්
household_portion: Building from 3–4 tsp towards 5–6 tsp twice daily
energy_enrichment: Tempered with a little bit of pure vegetable oil
preparation_steps: Boil chicken breast until tender.
Mince and shred finely.
Cook red rice and dhal until soft.
Temper with 1/2 tsp vegetable oil.
Mash together smoothly to a semi-solid paste.
safety_precautions: Mince chicken very fine to prevent choking.
developmental_rationale: Chicken provides easily digestible animal protein and zinc for cellular growth and immunity.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Chicken introduced on days 7 to 9 as animal-origin food.

name: 4-Part Mash: Rice, Dhal, Sprats & Yellow Pumpkin
sinhala_name: පරිප්පු, හාල්මැස්සන්, වට්ටක්කා සමඟ බත් (4-කොටස් මිශ්‍රණය)
household_portion: 5 to 6 teaspoons at a time, twice a day + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_steps: Peel pumpkin and cut into small cubes.
Combine rice, dhal, pumpkin, and 1 tsp FHB sprat powder in a cooking pot.
Add thick coconut milk and boil until all components are soft and tender.
Mash together smoothly with a clean spoon.
Serve warm, followed by 1–2 tsp of mashed fruit.
developmental_rationale: Combines all 4 foundational food groups (staple + pulse + animal food + yellow vegetable) providing protein, iron, and provitamin A.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 10 to 15 4-part mash: 5–6 tsp twice a day + 1–2 tsp fruit.

name: 4-Part Mash: Rice, Green Gram, Liver & Carrot
sinhala_name: මුං ඇට, අක්මාව, කැරට් සමඟ බත්
household_portion: 5 to 6 teaspoons at a time, twice a day + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_steps: Boil green gram and red rice soft.
Cook liver thoroughly until tender, mince finely.
Boil peeled carrot soft and mash.
Combine with thick coconut milk and mash together into a soft semi-solid paste.
safety_precautions: Ensure liver is cooked thoroughly and minced finely.
developmental_rationale: Liver and carrot provide exceptionally concentrated bioavailable iron and vitamin A for red blood cell synthesis and immune protection.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 10 to 15: liver and carrot included as animal food and yellow vegetable in 4-part mash.

name: 4-Part Mash: Rice, Cowpea, Fish & Sweet Potato
sinhala_name: කවුපි, මාළු, බතල සමඟ බත්
household_portion: 5 to 6 teaspoons at a time, twice a day + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_steps: Boil cowpea until tender.
Steam sea fish and debone with extreme care.
Boil peeled yellow sweet potato and rice until soft.
Combine all components with thick coconut milk and mash thoroughly.
developmental_rationale: Cowpea and sea fish provide complementary proteins and omega-3 fatty acids for cognitive and physical development.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Cowpea and yellow sweet potato featured in 4-part mash on days 10 to 15.

name: Half-Mashed Rice with Dhal, Egg Yolk & Gotukola
sinhala_name: බිත්තර කහ මදය, ගොටුකොළ සහ පරිප්පු සමඟ බත්
household_portion: About 1/4 of a tea cup at a time, 2 to 3 times a day + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_steps: Boil egg hard, separate yolk, and mash half of the boiled yolk.
Wash gotukola leaves thoroughly, chop very fine, and stir into cooked warm dhal and rice.
Cook with thick coconut milk until soft.
Half-mash the rice so texture progresses from smooth puree to small tender granules.
safety_precautions: Egg yolk only (egg white is not introduced until about 1 week later).
Offer sips of boiled cooled water after meal.
developmental_rationale: Gotukola introduces green leafy vegetables for folate and minerals, while egg yolk provides choline, lutein, and healthy fats.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 16 to 30: half-mashed rice (~1/4 tea cup), green leaves, and boiled egg yolk introduction.

name: Half-Mashed Rice with Sprat Powder, Murunga Leaves & Pumpkin
sinhala_name: හාල්මැස්සන්, මුරුංගා කොළ, වට්ටක්කා සමඟ බත්
household_portion: About 1/4 of a tea cup at a time, 2 to 3 times a day
preparation_steps: Strip tender murunga leaflets, wash thoroughly.
Cook red rice, dhal, pumpkin, and murunga leaves with thick coconut milk.
Add 1 tsp FHB sprat powder.
Half-mash with spoon, leaving small soft granules to stimulate chewing motions.
safety_precautions: Ensure murunga stems are discarded completely.
Fine sprat powder without sharp bones.
developmental_rationale: Murunga leaves and whole sprats create an iron- and calcium-dense meal that prevents childhood nutritional anemia.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Murunga leaves and sprats in half-mashed rice during days 16 to 30.

name: Coarsely Mashed Rice with Sea Fish, Dhal & Sarana
sinhala_name: මාළු, පරිප්පු, සාරණ සමඟ කැකුළු බත්
household_portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2 to 3 times a day + 2 to 3 teaspoons fruit
preparation_steps: Cook white rice and dhal soft with thick coconut milk.
Steam sea fish and debone meticulously.
Cook sarana leaves until tender, chop fine.
Coarsely mash all components together with a clean fork or spoon.
developmental_rationale: At 7 completed months, texture advances to coarsely mashed to develop tongue control and chewing coordination.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months completed: 1/2 tea cup, 2 to 3 times a day, coarsely mashed texture.

name: Coarsely Mashed Rice with Germinated Soya & Whole Egg
sinhala_name: සෝයා සහ බිත්තර සමඟ බත්
household_portion: 1/2 tea cup, 2 to 3 times a day + about 4 teaspoons fruit + 1–2 snacks
preparation_steps: Boil germinated soya soft and mash coarsely.
Hard-boil egg, mash both yolk and white coarsely (eligible only after yolk previously tolerated).
Cook red rice and thampala leaves with thick coconut milk.
Combine all items into a coarse mash.
safety_precautions: Prerequisite check: Egg yolk must have been introduced and tolerated prior to offering whole egg.
developmental_rationale: Introduces whole egg at 7 months and 1 week once yolk is established, providing complete protein for muscle building.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months and 1 week: coarsely mashed rice with germinated soya and whole egg.

name: Coarsely Chopped Boiled Jak with Dhal & Sprats
sinhala_name: තැම්බූ කොස්, පරිප්පු සහ හාල්මැස්සන්
household_portion: A bit more than 1/2 tea cup, 2 to 3 times a day + ~1/4 tea cup fruit + 1–2 snacks
preparation_steps: Boil young jak (kos) soft in thick coconut milk.
Coarsely chop into soft chewable pieces.
Prepare soft dhal curry with 1 tsp sprat powder.
Combine coarsely chopped jak with dhal and sprats.
safety_precautions: Ensure jak is cooked completely soft so baby can chew easily with gums.
No salt or sugar before 1 year.
developmental_rationale: Introduces traditional Sri Lankan root/tuber staple foods to diversify palate and develop rotary chewing.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 8 completed months: traditional staples like boiled jak (kos), coarsely chopped, portion a bit more than 1/2 tea cup.

name: Coarsely Chopped Breadfruit with Fish Curry & Dhal
sinhala_name: තැම්බූ දෙල් සහ මාළු හොදි
household_portion: A bit more than 1/2 tea cup, 2 to 3 times a day
preparation_steps: Peel breadfruit rind, cut into cubes, boil soft in coconut milk.
Coarsely chop boiled breadfruit.
Steam sea fish, debone with care, and mix with mild dhal curry.
Serve coarsely chopped breadfruit coated with fish and dhal.
safety_precautions: Ensure breadfruit is soft enough to squish between thumb and forefinger.
developmental_rationale: Breadfruit provides high energy and dietary variety from traditional Sri Lankan food sources.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled breadfruit (del) introduced at 8 completed calendar months.

name: String Hoppers with Dhal Curry & Steamed Fish
sinhala_name: ඉඳිආප්ප, පරිප්පු සහ මාළු
household_portion: A bit more than 1/2 tea cup (8m) scaling to 3/4 cup (9–11m) and >1 cup (12m+)
preparation_steps: Steam fresh string hoppers.
Cut or chop string hoppers into small bite-sized strands.
Pour thick coconut milk dhal curry over string hoppers to soften.
Debone steamed fish thoroughly and flake into the dish.
safety_precautions: No salt added if child is under 1 year.
developmental_rationale: Popular Sri Lankan family meal format that encourages self-feeding and table food integration.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: String hoppers featured as staple at 8 months and throughout weekly matrix.

name: Rice with Chicken, Dhal & Nivithi (Served Separately)
sinhala_name: වෙන් වෙන්ව බෙදූ බත්, කුකුල් මස්, පරිප්පු සහ නිවිති
household_portion: 3/4 tea cup of food at a time (a bit more at 9m), 3 to 4 times a day + 1 to 2 snacks
energy_enrichment: Coconut milk in dhal and spinach curries
preparation_steps: Cook white rice soft.
Prepare separate mild curries: tender shredded chicken, creamy dhal, and chopped spinach (nivithi).
FHB Separate Serving Style: Serve rice and each curry separately on the child's plate.
Mix portions together with clean fingers or spoon while feeding to let the child explore distinct colors and tastes.
developmental_rationale: Serving curries separately stimulates visual curiosity and palate discrimination, preventing feeding aversion.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 9 to 11 months: rice and curries served separately on plate and mixed while feeding; portion 3/4 tea cup.

name: Rice with Whole Sprat Curry, Dhal & Drumstick Pods Pulp
sinhala_name: බත්, හාල්මැස්සන් හොදි, පරිප්පු සහ මුරුංගා කරල්
household_portion: 3/4 tea cup at each meal, 3 to 4 times a day + 1 to 2 snacks
preparation_steps: Cook red rice soft.
Prepare sprat curry using fine whole sprat powder or soft whole sprats with soft heads.
Cook drumstick pods (murunga karal) tender; scrape out the soft pulp and tender seeds, discarding the fibrous woody skin.
Serve rice, dhal, sprat curry, and drumstick pulp separately on plate and mix while feeding.
safety_precautions: Discard fibrous outer skin of drumstick pods.
developmental_rationale: High calcium and iron meal from whole sprats and drumstick pulp supporting skeletal mineralization.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: FHB 9–11 months plate: separate serving style, 3–4 meals daily, 3/4 tea cup.

name: Family Table: Rice, Sea Fish Curry, Watakolu & Mukunuwenna
sinhala_name: බත්, මාළු හොදි, වැටකොළු සහ මුකුණුවැන්න මැල්ලුම
household_portion: A bit more than 1 tea cup (1–2y) scaling to close to 2 tea cups (2–5y)
energy_enrichment: Cooked with coconut milk and fresh scraped coconut
preparation_steps: Prepare wholesome family meal: boiled rice, mild fish curry in coconut milk, ridge gourd (watakolu) curry, and mukunuwenna mallum.
Debone fish portion carefully before serving child.
Ensure child receives: 2 vegetables + 1 green leafy vegetable daily as per FHB guidelines.
safety_precautions: Keep chili level mild for young children.
developmental_rationale: Fulfills the FHB 1–5 years daily rule: two vegetables + one green leafy vegetable + animal protein.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 1 to 5 years: nutritious family food, 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks, two vegetables + one green leaf daily.

name: Family Table: Rice with Roasted Kunisso, Dhal & Gotukola
sinhala_name: බත්, කූනිස්සන් බැදුම, පරිප්පු සහ ගොටුකොළ
household_portion: A bit more than 1 tea cup (1–2y), kunisso 2 tablespoons per day
energy_enrichment: Coconut milk dhal and scraped coconut mallum
preparation_steps: Wash kunisso thoroughly to remove grit, roast or sauté lightly.
Measure 2 tablespoons of cooked kunisso for the child.
Serve with red rice, creamy dhal curry, and gotukola mallum with scraped coconut.
developmental_rationale: Kunisso provides concentrated minerals, protein, and calcium in an affordable traditional Sri Lankan form.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Kunisso (2 tablespoons per day) specified in the FHB daily food requirements table for 1–5 years.

name: Milk Rice with Sea Fish & Dhal Curry
sinhala_name: කිරිබත්, මාළු සහ පරිප්පු
household_portion: A bit more than 1 tea cup (1–2y) scaling to 1.5–2 tea cups
energy_enrichment: Cooked with rich thick coconut milk
preparation_steps: Cook white rice soft, add thick coconut milk with a pinch of salt (after 1 year), and simmer until creamy milk rice (kiribath) forms.
Cut into soft diamonds.
Serve with mild fish curry (deboned) and dhal curry.
safety_precautions: Only for children aged 12 months or older.
developmental_rationale: Featured in the FHB weekly meal matrix for Monday breakfast, providing high energy and traditional cultural familiarity.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Milk rice with fish featured as Monday breakfast in the FHB weekly meal planning matrix.

name: High-Protein Vegetarian Meal: Rice with Dhal, Chickpeas & Pumpkin
sinhala_name: පරිප්පු, කඩල සහ වට්ටක්කා සමඟ බත්
household_portion: 1/2 to 3/4 tea cup according to age stage
preparation_steps: Boil dhal and soaked chickpeas until very soft.
Cook pumpkin tender with thick coconut milk.
Combine with soft rice and mash coarsely.
Provides dual-pulse plant protein for vegetarian households.
safety_precautions: Ensure chickpeas are mashed thoroughly to prevent choking.
developmental_rationale: Nutritious plant-protein meal combining lentils, chickpeas, and pumpkin in a coarsely mashed texture.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Derived vegetarian meal combination using FHB Tier A pulse and vegetable recommendations for non-meat households.
